one_line: A shared, permissioned itinerary edited through a browser agent on a live map.
what_it_does: Provides shared trip itineraries with separate read-only and edit links, letting an agent search places, compute travel time, and update the visible map and plan.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the agent shares live map context, has permission-scoped tools, and changes structured itinerary state while the human sees the same map. Generic UI driving would be materially less reliable and precise.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description make agent conversation the only edit UI.
Separate edit/view URLs expose different tool sets and server-enforced permissions.
Frame sheets show agent panel alongside a changing map with markers and result panels.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent map workflow with agent-side activity and changing map state; the scope is focused and intentional, though the contact sheets do not prove every itinerary operation end to end.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion sheets show the map, agent panel, controls, markers, and successive states.
Description specifies structured itinerary decisions, live travel facts, activity logging, and revocable links.
impact_rationale: Travel companions and families have a concrete need for shared planning with permissions and current travel context; the product addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Shared road-trip itinerary and view/edit collaboration are clearly described.
Visible map workflow connects search, routing, and itinerary context.
creativity_rationale: A no-edit-UI itinerary whose permissions are granted by sharing a URL and whose agent operates in the same map is a memorable, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Conversation is intentionally the editing surface.
Permission-scoped WebMCP worlds and live map confirmation are unusual and specific.
usability_note: Shared map context and visible activity confirmation are strong; conversational-only editing may be unfamiliar.
standouts: Live map and itinerary shared state
advance_reason: High WebMCP delta, strong visible product motion, and a distinctive collaboration model.

one_line: A hotel operations system whose reservations and housekeeping workflows are exposed as domain-specific agent tools.
what_it_does: Manages rooms, reservations, guests, check-in/out, housekeeping status, occupancy, and revenue for hotel staff, with validated WebMCP operations.
leverage_rationale: Structured hotel-domain tools with validation and business-rule enforcement are substantially safer and more reliable than generic browser automation for operational tasks, though the UI already supports the same workflows.
leverage_evidence: Description lists purpose-built reservation, room, guest, and reporting tools.
Overlapping reservations and unavailable rooms are rejected by the application.
Frames visibly pair the hotel dashboard with a WebMCP Tools/interact panel.
execution_rationale: The dashboard is coherent and appears implemented, but the frames mostly show a static restaurant page and tool panel rather than a completed hotel reservation flow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a polished hotel-management dashboard with navigation, metrics, filters, and tool panel.
No clearly visible completed reservation, check-in, or status mutation in the sheets.
impact_rationale: Hotel owners and staff have frequent, concrete operational workflows where reliable structured actions can save time and prevent booking errors.
impact_evidence: Clearly defined hotel staff audience and operational use cases.
Business rules address real reservation and room-status risks.
creativity_rationale: An agent-operable PMS is a useful synthesis, but the underlying category and interaction model are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Domain-specific WebMCP tools rather than generic database calls.
Concept remains a conventional hotel PMS with agent access.
usability_note: Operational dashboard is legible; evidence does not show the complete agent workflow.
red_flags: Motion evidence appears largely static and may not demonstrate the claimed core flow.
advance_reason: Credible high-impact operational concept with visible implementation, despite thin end-to-end video evidence.

one_line: A browser agent turns a drafted message into paid, physical mail.
what_it_does: Lets an agent prepare letters or postcards, upload material, create payment, check status, and cancel orders through PieterPost fulfillment.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects drafting, document preparation, payment handoff, and fulfillment status in one structured conversation; generic automation would require brittle multi-step form driving.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools span upload, preparation, payment link, status, cancellation, and order listing.
Description explicitly contrasts the multi-step agent workflow with manual copy, forms, uploads, and return visits.
Frames show a checkout/payment state transitioning to a blue order-prepared confirmation state.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates a coherent transaction transition from checkout to confirmation, and the described tool set covers the workflow with safety features.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows payment form and repeated post-submit order/status confirmation UI.
Description reports strict schemas, cancellation, retries, and existing fulfillment integration.
impact_rationale: Individuals and small businesses have real needs to send invoices, documents, cancellations, and personal mail; the solution removes substantial friction while retaining payment control.
impact_evidence: Concrete use cases include invoices, cancellation requests, documents, and cards.
Payment and recipient controls remain with the person.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to bridge AI-generated text to a physical mailbox is a fresh and memorable extension of agent action.
creativity_evidence: Prompt-to-post interaction crosses from digital generation into physical fulfillment.
Structured fulfillment status is part of the same agent workflow.
usability_note: The workflow is naturally conversational and ends in a clear confirmation state.
advance_reason: Strong visible transaction evidence and unusually tangible WebMCP value.

one_line: A shared job-search board where agents research and draft while humans approve state changes.
what_it_does: Searches and scores jobs, drafts tailored applications, advances a pipeline, and records notes in a human-controlled workspace.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on the same live board and staged approval feed as the person, making structured shared state and safe approvals central rather than cosmetic.
leverage_evidence: Description defines shared live page state and pending actions requiring human approval.
Tools cover job search, scoring, drafting, pipeline movement, and notes.
Packet includes multiple product-motion sheets and a full workspace description.
execution_rationale: The product surfaces are coherent and ambitious, but the available evidence does not clearly show an end-to-end approved application submission.
execution_evidence: Description lays out Job Board, Tracker, Profile & Docs, and WebMCP areas.
Frame packet provides product UI motion, but the core approval result is not legible enough to verify fully.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face repetitive research and application work, and human approval is an appropriate safeguard for consequential submissions.
impact_evidence: Clear audience and recurring job-search pain point.
One-click approval preserves user ownership while delegating tedious work.
creativity_rationale: The shared activity feed and staged agent actions create a thoughtful human-agent collaboration pattern beyond a cover-letter chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human work the same page and document.
Every state-changing action is pending until approved.
usability_note: Workspace organization and approval gates support trust, though the workflow is information-dense.
red_flags: No transcript and limited legibility of the exact agent result.
advance_reason: High audience value and strong collaboration design with credible product evidence.

one_line: A chessboard-aware agent coach teaches through live annotations instead of only giving engine moves.
what_it_does: Reads the live position, evaluates it with local Stockfish, and displays hints, highlights, arrows, candidate lines, and coaching messages.
leverage_rationale: The agent can inspect structured board state and write visual teaching annotations into the exact live board; ordinary UI driving is less precise and less pedagogically expressive.
leverage_evidence: Tool list includes get_board_state, evaluate_position, history, highlights, arrows, candidate lines, and coach messages.
Description emphasizes reading, analysis, explanation, and visual teaching as one loop.
Frame packet shows the chess product and agent/tool interaction context.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and technically coherent, with a local engine and a complete set of teaching actions; frame evidence supports a real chess interface though not every tool call.
execution_evidence: Description specifies local Stockfish WASM and legal continuation handling.
Product-motion evidence shows the interactive chess experience and changing instructional overlays.
impact_rationale: Beginner and intermediate players have a clear learning need, and visual explanations address a known weakness of raw engine output.
impact_evidence: Concrete learner questions and Elo-aware coaching use cases.
Hints and arrows teach ideas without necessarily revealing the answer.
creativity_rationale: Turning an agent into a visual, board-native teacher is a strong interaction concept rather than a generic chess chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Agent writes pedagogical annotations directly onto the board.
Candidate-line and hint modes support graduated instruction.
usability_note: Visual board annotations make feedback actionable and understandable.
advance_reason: Strong educational fit, coherent implementation, and meaningful structured-state advantage.

one_line: A structured DBS research workbench for searching, comparing, planning, and exporting cited evidence.
what_it_does: Lets researchers and agents search a curated set of deep-brain-stimulation studies, compare protocols, build and save plans, and export cited briefs, with live Europe PMC search.
leverage_rationale: Persistent structured outputs chain from search to comparison to plan, avoiding re-parsed chat prose and preserving shared researcher-agent state.
leverage_evidence: Six tools are wired to the same functions as page buttons.
Description explicitly gives a search_studies → compare_protocols → build_research_plan chain.
Frames show a research workbench with agent/tool context.
execution_rationale: The stated workbench has a focused workflow, curated evidence boundary, persistent plans, and export; the packet shows product motion but not every export step.
execution_evidence: Description specifies 14 verified studies, unreviewed live search labeling, saved plans, and cited export.
Frame sheets show the research application and successive UI states.
impact_rationale: Researchers in a specialized clinical domain have a real evidence-synthesis problem, and structured comparison can reduce fragmented searching while clearly labeling evidence quality.
impact_evidence: Concrete DBS programming research audience and scattered-literature problem.
Curated studies and explicit unreviewed labeling support responsible use.
creativity_rationale: The combination of evidence triangulation, persistent chained tools, and a shared research plan is a fresh, domain-specific agent interaction.
creativity_evidence: Workbench rather than transient chatbot answers.
Structured outputs become inputs to subsequent research tools.
usability_note: Structured workflows and evidence labels help; the specialized domain may require onboarding.
red_flags: Clinical research claims warrant careful distinction between research support and medical advice.
standouts: Curated plus clearly marked live literature
advance_reason: Strong domain fit and credible structured-research workflow.

one_line: A one-line runtime that lets voice and gesture drive a site's existing WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Adds voice, hand-gesture, and text clients to WebMCP tools, with a shop demo, trace panel, injector CLI, and Claude Code integration.
leverage_rationale: The product treats a site's declared tool layer as a reusable capability surface for multiple human modalities, avoiding brittle synthetic clicks and extending WebMCP beyond chat agents.
leverage_evidence: Description says voice and gesture are clients of the same tools, with no LLM in the loop.
One-line runtime, idempotent injector, tool auditing, confirmation gates, and trace panel are described.
Two frame sheets show agent/product tooling and the connected experience.
execution_rationale: The concept and integration surface are unusually broad and appear implemented, but the packet has only two frame sheets and limited legible proof of the full voice/gesture loop.
execution_evidence: Description specifies demo shop tools, runtime, plugin, injector, and verification flow.
Frame sheets show product/tooling UI, though completed multimodal actions are not clearly readable.
impact_rationale: Developers can add accessible alternative input and agents to existing sites with low integration cost; the approach also benefits hands-busy or accessibility-focused users.
impact_evidence: One command plus one script line is a concrete developer value proposition.
Voice and camera input reuse site capabilities rather than duplicating action logic.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP as a modality-neutral action layer for voice and hand gestures, explicitly without an LLM, is a novel and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Three clients share the same declared tools.
Gesture control and tool auditing are pursued as a reusable runtime, not a one-off demo.
usability_note: Low integration cost is compelling; multimodal recognition and permission UX remain potential friction.
red_flags: Only two frame sheets and no transcript limit direct verification of voice/gesture execution.
advance_reason: Highly original infrastructure concept with substantial potential leverage despite thin video proof.

one_line: A dating experience where a user's AI offers contextual opinions before the user decides to connect.
what_it_does: Combines photo-first profile browsing with agent-assisted context, onboarding, likes, matching, and messaging while keeping the user in control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP bridges the user's private AI context and the exact dating profile currently viewed, enabling a defined review-and-act loop that generic UI automation cannot safely reproduce as well.
leverage_evidence: Agent can read the current candidate and its own user's Agent Profile through page tools.
Likes record the agent opinion and user retains the decision.
Frames show profile browsing plus agent-oriented interface states.
execution_rationale: The concept has clear states and safety framing, but evidence does not fully demonstrate matching and messaging end to end.
execution_evidence: Description specifies onboarding, ordered photos, Agent Profiles, likes, mutual matches, and messaging.
Three frame sheets show the product browsing experience and agent panel.
impact_rationale: Dating users have a real desire for better context and thoughtful decision support, though the value is inherently subjective and privacy-sensitive.
impact_evidence: Specific pain point: photos do not convey communication style or expectations.
User control and limited contextual Agent Profiles are explicit safeguards.
creativity_rationale: Sharing a personal AI's contextual understanding with a dating site, while attaching the opinion to a Like, is a notably original social interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent opinion becomes part of reciprocal matching context.
Profiles include familiarity duration and interaction density with expiration.
usability_note: Photo-first browsing is familiar; AI-mediated intimacy and privacy require careful trust design.
red_flags: Privacy, consent, and interpretation risks are material in dating contexts.
standouts: Opinion attached to the matching decision
advance_reason: Original, socially relevant interaction with credible safeguards and visible product evidence.

one_line: A visible browser-agent orchestrator assembles specialist crews to complete bounded creative missions.
what_it_does: Discovers scenarios and agent presets, configures a crew and turn budget, runs observable turns over a shared 3D artifact, and summarizes collaboration quality.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides typed, bounded orchestration over a visible multi-agent simulation: the agent discovers valid IDs, configures state, advances turns, and reads structured results while the human watches the same artifact.
leverage_evidence: Description lists discovery, configuration, preview, run, and analysis tools.
Each turn exposes messages, action types, metrics, and 3D artifact changes.
Frame sheets show the assembly lab, crew, and result-oriented UI.
execution_rationale: The bounded mission and observable turn-by-turn workflow are unusually well specified and appear coherent, though full completion is not fully legible in every frame.
execution_evidence: Description defines fixed turn budgets, validated IDs, preview, run, and structured analysis.
Three motion sheets show the product's crew/assembly experience and evolving result views.
impact_rationale: Players, educators, and agent designers can use it to explore collaboration and creative orchestration; the value is real but more experimental than operational.
impact_evidence: Visible specialist crew and shared artifact make collaboration inspectable.
Structured grades, observations, and recommendations support learning and evaluation.
creativity_rationale: A browser agent assembling and supervising a visible creative crew in a 3D mission, with inspectable turns and collaboration metrics, is exceptionally original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Agent orchestration is the core play loop, not an assistant bolted onto a game.
Turn-by-turn shared artifact and collaboration analysis pursue the idea deeply.
usability_note: Bounded missions and previews make a complex multi-agent experience inspectable.
red_flags: Submission distinguishes a pre-existing sandbox from the new judged WebMCP extension; score the extension only.
standouts: Bounded typed turns with shared 3D state
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and transformative structured orchestration with strong packet evidence.

one_line: A cyber incident-response simulation where the page enforces safe, explainable agent actions.
what_it_does: Lets a player and agent investigate a staged breach, read evidence, propose actions, approve them, and progress through a stateful incident console with receipts.
leverage_rationale: Safety-critical sequencing and page-enforced consequences make structured site tools substantially more capable than pixel-driving; the page is the referee and preserves what changed and why.
leverage_evidence: Description contrasts tool guarantees with unsafe clicking and specifies order, cost, and consequence.
Seven tools expose incident state, evidence, proposals, and actions with failure explanations.
Frame sheets show the cyber console, agent context, and changing simulation states.
execution_rationale: The simulation has a clear narrative, state machine, approval model, receipts, and failure recovery; video supports the product and progression, though not every branch.
execution_evidence: Description specifies shift gating, visible receipts, safe failures, and exactly one way forward.
Three motion sheets show the incident-response interface and product state changes.
impact_rationale: Security learners and practitioners need practice with sequencing and consequences; the simulation teaches operational reasoning without real-world risk.
impact_evidence: Concrete SOC scenario and realistic session-revocation/password-reset sequencing.
Page-refereed actions make consequences and evidence visible.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP as a safety and accountability layer for an interactive incident-response simulation is a strong, memorable use of the medium.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes and human approves while the page enforces domain rules.
Receipts explain what happened, what changed, and why it mattered.
usability_note: Narrative console, approvals, and receipts make a complex security scenario learnable.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP fit with strong educational impact, distinctive safety model, and credible motion evidence.
